setup.data: Inputs of 30 MTEB tasks: 13 classification (e.g. Banking77, Imdb, MTOP), 11 retrieval (e.g. NQ, HotpotQA, SciFact, FiQA2018), 6 other (2 reranking, 2 STS, 2 duplicate detection). Each layer's token states are pooled to one vector per example with the official or model-recommended pooling 'when available'; no rule is given for models without one (e.g. the base LLMs). N per task is not stated; NRS uses up to 500 anchors. No factual-failure, pressure or behaviour labels.
setup.models: 31 models: 13 encoder embedders (MiniLM 6 layers to BERT-large-based 24 layers), 12 decoder embedders (8 Mistral-7B-based, BGE-multilingual-gemma2 on Gemma-2-9B with 42 layers, GTE-Qwen2-7B, Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and 8B), 6 base LLMs (Falcon-7B, Gemma-2-2B, GPT-2, GPT-2 XL, Llama-3.2-1B, Mistral-7B-v0.1). Largest is about 9B.
setup.layers_positions: All layers 0..L on one pooled vector per example (not per token). Frenet: subspace per layer = top-r right singular vectors of the centered N x d matrix X_l, with r = smallest rank explaining 95% of final-layer variance, the same r at every layer.
setup.method_in_one_line: Three separate layer-wise measure families: Frenet (Grassmann geodesic speed between adjacent layers, Menger curvature over consecutive triples, end-to-end displacement d_{0,L}); NRS (Jaccard overlap of each anchor's 20 nearest neighbours between adjacent layers); GFMI (mutual information between each layer's and the final layer's kNN-graph component partitions, integrated over a percentile filtration).
setup.baselines: Model selection: none head-to-head (stated omission); quality references are official MTEB scores (25 embedders) and MMLU (6 base LLMs). Layer pruning: Random removal (3 seeds) and last-k removal, on a separate panel of 5 models (BGE-base-en-v1.5, E5-large-v2, Nemotron-Embed-1B, LLM2Vec-Mistral-7B, Mistral-7B-v0.1) x 3 tasks (AmazonPolarity, FiQA2018, STSBenchmark) = 15 cells, with one base LLM only (p. 8 footnote 1). Nemotron-Embed-1B and LLM2Vec-Mistral-7B are not in the 31-model panel of Table B.1.
setup.controls: Per-task Spearman with count of significant tasks; task-type stratification; MMLU panel as a directional check across model classes; fixed hyperparameters (kNRS 20, kGFMI 30, 20 percentile points over [5, 95], 95% variance rule); first and last three layers protected in pruning; mean and median reported. Missing: control for embedding dimension, depth or family in the selection correlations; any causal test beyond block skipping.
setup.compute: Four NVIDIA V100 (32 GB); about 300 GPU-hours for all measurement and pruning experiments. Forward passes only, no training.

figures.what_is_plotted: Per family: number of models, normalized depth of the curvature peak d_peak(kappa), and late-minus-early NRS trend Delta J.
figures.takeaway: Family means: decoder embedders and base LLMs bend their population subspace late and stabilise neighbourhoods late; encoder embedders have a mid-depth mean peak and flat Delta J. The means hide wide spreads: encoder peaks run 0.08 (E5) to 0.99 (Snowflake) (Table C.3), the decoder-embedder 0.89 is driven by 8 Mistral-7B fine-tunes with near-identical peaks (0.867-0.868), and the base-LLM late peak holds for 5 of 6 models (GPT-2 peaks at 0.38).
figures.numbers: Encoder 13 models, d_peak 0.56, Delta J +0.015; decoder embedder 12, 0.89, +0.144; base LLM 6, 0.78, +0.121.

key_results.claim: Only the final-layer-alignment rule (GFMI) beats random layer skipping at higher budgets.
key_results.quote: For pruning, GFMI is the only measurement-guided rule that beats Random at the 15% and 20% budgets and has the best median change at every budget.

key_results.claim: Grassmann-motion pruning works only for light budgets; neighbourhood-stability does not transfer from selection to pruning.
key_results.quote: Frenet is effective only at the lightest budget, while NRS does not transfer from model selection to pruning.

key_results.claim: End-to-end subspace displacement d_{0,L} is the strongest of the paper's three LRD scores for ranking embedders by MTEB quality. No external label-free or transferability baseline was tested (stated omission, p. 9), so 'best label-free predictor' is not shown.
key_results.quote: For selection, all three model-level scores correlate positively with downstream MTEB performance, with end-to-end subspace displacement (d0,L ) the strongest

key_results.claim: Grassmann subspace rank r is fixed from the final layer and reused for every layer.
key_results.quote: we fix the subspace dimension r as the smallest rank that explains 95% of the variance of the final-layer representation XL

key_results.claim: Where the subspace path bends most depends on architecture: late in decoder models (family means; 5 of 6 base LLMs peak late, GPT-2 at 0.38; decoder-embedder mean driven by 8 Mistral-7B fine-tunes).
key_results.quote: Curvature peak depth dpeak (κ) separates the three families: encoder embedders peak at mid-depth, whereas decoder embedders and base LLMs peak later (Table 1).

key_results.claim: Local neighbourhoods settle late in decoder models.
key_results.quote: Encoder embedders are nearly flat (∆J ≈ 0.01), while in decoder embedders and base LLMs the local neighborhoods stabilize toward later layers.

key_results.claim: Task type shifts trajectory shape only slightly: curvature differences are in the third decimal (e.g. 0.137 vs 0.132), smaller than the within-family spread (decoder-embedder curvature 0.103-0.150 across models, Table C.3), and the retrieval claim has exceptions (Table 2).
key_results.quote: classification has higher mean curvature in the encoder and decoder families, with base LLMs showing little task-type difference, whereas retrieval has higher mean speed and GFMI scale.
With n = 6 this panel resolves only large effects, so we report it as a directional generalization check.
by mean, it improves over Random at 15% (−2.37% vs −5.90%) and 20% (−6.14% vs −12.08%).

key_results.claim: Low Grassmann speed and curvature do not mean a layer is safe to remove at larger budgets.
key_results.quote: the Frenet rule is competitive at the lightest budget (−2.10% mean at 5%, the lowest of any rule) but degrades rapidly as the budget grows (−21.33% at 20%).

key_results.claim: Geometric stability of a layer is not the same as causal dispensability.
key_results.quote: the per-layer rule z(Jl ) does not carry over to pruning, since a layer that does not change local neighborhoods is not necessarily dispensable.

key_results.claim: The paper's text says only that on LLMs the rules are hard to separate from Random. Table D.6 (p. 26, Mistral-7B-v0.1, 3 tasks) shows no rule clearly beats Random: task means Random -12.7 / +8.9 / +8.3 / -9.1 vs GFMI -11.8 / -20.6 / +2.3 / -10.6 at 5/10/15/20% (our recomputation), with cells from -83% to +65%, so n = 3 is noise.
key_results.quote: The GFMI advantage is concentrated at higher budgets and is largest on encoder embedders. On LLMs the three rules are harder to separate from Random.

key_results.claim: Base LLMs have more curved, slower subspace paths than embedders.
key_results.quote: Base LLMs have higher mean curvature and GFMI scale, lower mean speed, and substantial within-family spread

key_results.claim: Subspace motion and graph alignment carry different information.
key_results.quote: Final-layer graph alignment therefore captures structure beyond subspace displacement.

methods.name: Frenet: Grassmann geodesic speed, Menger curvature and end-to-end displacement
methods.what_it_measures: Per layer, the top-r PCA subspace of the centered example cloud (N x d), r fixed by 95% of final-layer variance. Speed s_l = sqrt(sum of squared principal angles) between layers l and l+1; Menger curvature from the triangle (Heron's formula) of three consecutive layers; d_{0,L} = distance from input to output subspace.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Population-level only, so no per-item fate. Run separately on the neutral and pushback item sets (or on flipped vs resisted items matched on prior confidence), it can show at which layer the two populations' subspace paths separate and whether the pushback path bends (curvature spike) at a specific layer; a between-condition distance that rises and stays high fits 5 transformed or 4 override at population level, a collapse of r-dim variance would hint at 6 erased. It cannot tell which.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Choose the layer of maximal between-condition distance or curvature for patching; or project pushback residuals onto the neutral subspace at that layer and see if the answer returns.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Cached pooled or answer-position residuals for a few hundred items per condition; SVD per layer; seconds to minutes. Note the paper's rule needs N > r.

methods.name: Neighborhood Retention Score (NRS): per-anchor kNN Jaccard between adjacent layers
methods.what_it_measures: For each anchor example, the Jaccard overlap of its 20 cosine nearest neighbours in layer l and l+1; averaged over up to 500 anchors.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: The one item-level piece in the paper. Adapted to compare an item's neighbours at the same layer under neutral vs pushback, it can ask whether a flipped item moved into the neighbourhood of items whose answer is the user's claim (4 override or 5 transformed into the other answer's region) or into a diffuse region with unstable neighbours (closer to 6 erased). Retention between conditions for resisted items is the control.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: Patch the item's neutral residual at the first layer where its neighbour set changes and test whether behaviour reverts.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Same cached residuals; kNN per layer; cheap.

methods.name: Graph Filtration Mutual Information (GFMI): alignment of each layer's kNN-graph partition with the final layer
methods.what_it_measures: For percentile thresholds 5-95 (20 points), connected components of the thresholded 30-NN cosine graph at layer l vs the final layer, compared by mutual information and integrated (AUC).
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Indirect. Swapping 'final-layer partition' for the behaviour label (flip vs resist) gives the earliest layer whose item geometry already predicts the outcome, which is a 'where does the fork appear' marker, not a fate. Raw MI is unbounded and family-dependent.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: None directly; it picked the least harmful layers to skip (pruning), which is a weak causal signal.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Cached residuals; kNN graphs and connected components over 20 thresholds per layer; cheap.

methods.name: Inference-time block skipping with Random and last-k baselines
methods.what_it_measures: Relative task-score change when chosen transformer blocks are skipped (no retraining), first/last 3 layers protected, budgets 5-20% of prunable layers.
methods.which_fate_it_could_diagnose: Crude causal localisation: skipping a layer band that carries the override should restore the correct answer under pushback; for 2 bypass, skipping the layers where the correct answer is decodable should leave behaviour unchanged. Random-layer skipping is the needed control.
methods.causal_followup_it_allows: It is itself the causal test; finer versions are sublayer ablation or patching.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Forward passes per budget and rule; cheap.

methods.name: Label-free model selection by Spearman correlation of geometric scores with benchmark scores
methods.what_it_measures: Whether a model-level geometric summary ranks models like a downstream benchmark.
methods.data_and_compute_needed: Many models; not relevant to us.

controls_worth_copying: For any 'this layer band matters' claim, compare against random layer choice (several seeds) and a last-k choice, and report both mean and median, since a few catastrophic cells dominate means.
Fix the subspace rank once by a rule (95% of final-layer variance) and reuse it at every layer so Grassmann distances are comparable across depth.
Keep global subspace motion, local neighbourhood change and alignment-to-final as separate measures; the paper shows they disagree (e.g. NRS works for selection but not for pruning).
Protect the first and last few layers in ablation sweeps so boundary effects do not drive results.
Report per-task significance counts, not only cross-task means.

pitfalls.pitfall: Random layer removal is a strong baseline; geometry-guided choice helped only past 10% and only for GFMI.
pitfalls.quote: Random is competitive at light budgets, and the measurement-guided prior is supported only for GFMI past the 10% budget.

pitfalls.pitfall: A geometrically stable layer is not necessarily causally unimportant (relevant to 'decodable is not used').
pitfalls.quote: the per-layer rule z(Jl ) does not carry over to pruning, since a layer that does not change local neighborhoods is not necessarily dispensable.

pitfalls.pitfall: Distance scales differ across layers, so thresholds must be per-layer percentiles, not shared absolute distances.
pitfalls.quote: Because edge-distance scales differ across layers, the threshold is parameterized by per-layer percentiles rather than by shared absolute distances

pitfalls.pitfall: The GFMI pruning rule is indirect: it does not measure what a block does.
pitfalls.quote: The GFMI criterion is indirect: it does not measure the block’s local transformation size but whether the layer’s graph organization already resembles the final-layer pattern.

pitfalls.pitfall: The geodesic distance sqrt(sum theta^2) grows with r, and r depends on each model's final-layer variance and width. d_{0,L} across models may partly track dimension or family rather than quality; Figure 1 shows two clusters of d_{0,L}, and the selection correlations have no control for width, depth or family. For us: when comparing conditions or models, use a fixed r and a normalized distance (e.g. mean cosine of principal angles).
All main measures are population-level (one subspace per layer over N examples); only NRS's per-anchor Jaccard is item-level. Pooling choice also changes X_l.
Relative score change is unstable when the unpruned score is small; Table D.6 contains large positive changes (up to about +65%) on some cells, likely on low-baseline base-LLM or retrieval cells.
Minor: the Mistral-7B citation [30] points to an unrelated 6G networks paper.

Pruning budgets collapse for small models: BGE-base (12 layers, 6 prunable) gives identical numbers at 5% and 10% and at 15% and 20% (Table D.6), so 'light budget' results (Frenet best at 5%, Random strong at 10%) partly reflect removing one layer in small models.

Menger curvature 4A/(abc) divides by the product of the three side lengths, so it is amplified where speed is tiny. If we reuse it on small between-condition distances, it will be noisy; report speed alongside it.

Family means hide spread and non-independence: encoder curvature peaks run 0.08-0.99, and 8 of the 12 decoder embedders are Mistral-7B fine-tunes with near-identical peaks (0.867-0.868), so the 0.89 family mean is not 12 independent points.

limitations_quote: The measurements also depend on input sampling, pooling, k-NN construction, and graph filtration percentile. Broader task coverage and stability analyses remain open.
future_work_quote: Spearman captures global rank agreement, and top-k selection quality is left to future work.

bears_on_fates.how: Per-anchor NRS Jaccard, adapted to compare an item's nearest neighbours at the same layer under neutral vs pushback, could show whether a flipped item relocates into the claimed answer's region (transformed or overridden) or loses stable neighbours (erased-like). The paper only compares adjacent layers on embedding tasks.

Grassmann speed and curvature computed separately per condition can locate the layer where a pressure condition's population subspace bends away from neutral, and compare that layer across pressure types. Population-level only; it cannot assign single items.

Block skipping is a crude causal tool, and the paper's finding that geometric stability does not imply dispensability is a reminder that 'decodable' and 'used' differ. No direct test of bypass or routing.

bears_on_fates.fate: H3 (probes trained on normal behaviour miss transformed/bypass)
bears_on_fates.how: Only an analogy: a layer-wise signal that works at one level (model selection) failed at another (pruning). No evidence about probes or failures.

bears_on_group_angle: The most explicit recipe in this wave for 'speed and curvature on the Grassmannian': top-r PCA subspace per layer with r fixed by the final layer, geodesic distance from principal angles, Menger curvature via Heron's formula over consecutive triples (zero for degenerate triples), end-to-end displacement. Finding that matters for where to look: decoder models bend their subspace path late (curvature peak at normalized depth 0.89 for decoder embedders and 0.78 for base LLMs; Mistral-7B-v0.1 0.856, Gemma-2-2B 0.901), and base LLMs have higher curvature and lower speed than embedders. This is directionally consistent with 2605.09011's late reorientation phase; qualitative only, since the objects (example-cloud PCA subspace on MTEB inputs vs lens-weight subspace on web text) and statistics (curvature peak vs RSS decline) differ. The late-bend evidence is n = 5 of 6 base LLMs (GPT-2 peaks at 0.38), and the decoder-embedder 0.89 is Mistral-driven. It also warns that one geometric summary is not enough: subspace motion, neighbourhood change and alignment-to-final are different events. No manifold vs linear steering, no between-condition comparison, no Procrustes.
architecture_location: Population subspace bends most in the last ~10-25% of depth in decoder models (Table 1; per-model peaks 0.74-0.92 for 5 of 6 base LLMs; GPT-2 peaks at 0.38; Table C.3; the decoder-embedder mean of 0.89 is driven by 8 Mistral-7B fine-tunes). Neighbourhoods stabilise in the last third (Delta J +0.12 to +0.14). Blocks already aligned with the final layer (high GFMI) are the least harmful to skip, but on the one base LLM tested no rule clearly beats random skipping (Table D.6, 3 tasks, noisy).
actionable_fix: None for safety. For us (our proposals, untested): (1) copy the Random-layer (3 seeds) and last-k baselines whenever we claim that patching or skipping a layer band changes a fate; (2) use the GFMI idea with behaviour labels to find the earliest layer whose item geometry already separates flip from resist, and intervene at or just before it; (3) use a normalized, fixed-r Grassmann distance between neutral and pushback item clouds per layer to pick the fork layer.
reuse_verdict: Reuse the Frenet formulas (speed, Menger curvature, fixed-r rule, but with a normalized distance) and the pruning baselines; adapt per-anchor NRS into a neutral-vs-pushback neighbour test. Skip GFMI-as-is and the model-selection study.
relevance_to_project: Low to medium. It studies embedding quality and pruning on MTEB, not failures, facts or causal mediation, and its main measures are population-level, so it cannot sort single items into fates. It is useful as a precise recipe for Grassmann speed and Menger curvature across layers, as evidence that decoder models bend their representation subspace late, and for one item-level tool (per-anchor kNN retention) we could turn into a between-condition test.
